title: Bivariate Bicycle Codes over Group Algebras
abstract: We study a weighted-shift formulation of bivariate bicycle group-algebra (BBGA) codes over finite group algebras. One binary shift acts by right multiplication and the other by left multiplication; associativity ensures that these shifts commute even for a nonabelian seed group. Bivariate polynomials in the shifts, including mixed monomials, therefore define CSS codes. We give explicit sparsity bounds and distinguish nonabelian seed groups from codes that are intrinsically inequivalent to abelian realizations. For $D_3$, a pair of weighted permutation shifts generates a regular $C_6\times C_{12}$ action and recovers the known $[[144,12,12]]$ and $[[144,14,14]]$ bivariate bicycle codes. We also present a computer-verified $[[144,16,12]]$ code over $A_4\times C_6$, with every check of weight eight. This example belongs to the established nonabelian two-block group-algebra family. Exhaustive low-weight enumeration and an intrinsic stabilizer-support invariant certify that it is inequivalent to any ordinary abelian BB or two-block group-algebra realization, even under qubit permutations combined with local Clifford operations. Finally, a nonuniform weighted-shift construction over $\mathbb{F}_2[C_3]$ yields a $[[18,4,3]]$ code with check weights six and eight. An exact enumeration of its minimum stabilizer supports rules out every ordinary binary 2BGA realization at that length, under the same equivalence. This establishes that the unrestricted weighted-shift formulation extends beyond the ordinary 2BGA class, even with an abelian seed group.
summary: This paper develops a weighted-shift framework for constructing Bivariate Bicycle Group-Algebra (BBGA) quantum codes over group algebras. It rigorously proves that certain constructed codes, particularly those derived from nonabelian or specific weighted-shift structures, cannot be equivalent to simpler, ordinary abelian realizations. This expands the known landscape of quantum error-correcting codes.
main_problem: The paper investigates Bivariate Bicycle Group-Algebra (BBGA) codes defined over finite group algebras, aiming to distinguish codes constructed via nonabelian group structures from those equivalent to simpler abelian realizations.
main_result: The authors construct specific quantum error-correcting codes, including one over $A_4 	imes C_6$ and another over $\mathbb{F}_2[C_3]$, which are proven to be inequivalent to any ordinary abelian 2BGA realization.
method: The construction relies on weighted-shift formulations using commuting shifts derived from left and right multiplications in the group algebra, leading to CSS codes defined by polynomial generators.
model_or_system: The model is quantum error correction using stabilizer codes defined over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[G]$ of a finite group $G$. Examples include $G=D_3$, $G=A_4 	imes C_6$, and $G=C_3$.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, check weights ($W_X, W_Z$), minimum stabilizer supports, and the automorphism group of the support graph $\Gamma$.
important_parameters: Code length $n=144$ and $n=18$; dimension $k=16$ and $k=4$; distance $d=12$ and $d=3$.
main_assumptions: The primary distinction is drawn between the general weighted-shift formulation and the restricted class of ordinary abelian 2BGA realizations.
figures_summary: The notes do not describe specific figures, but refer to tables summarizing known code parameters and the use of displayed formulas defining code generators.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general weighted-shift formulation for BBGA codes, presenting known examples (like those for $D_3$), constructing a specific nonabelian example ($A_4 	imes C_6$) and proving its inequivalence, and finally presenting a weighted-shift example ($C_3$) that extends beyond the ordinary abelian class.
why_interesting: This work advances the algebraic theory of quantum error-correcting codes by providing explicit constructions that challenge the boundaries of known equivalence classes, which is fundamental for designing robust quantum hardware.
